products.name: 2027 Budget Planner
products.promise: Plan every month, log what you spend, and see your whole year on one dashboard.
products.seo_description: A 2027 budget planner spreadsheet for Excel and Google Sheets: monthly budget vs actual, a 50/30/20 check and a yearly dashboard. Any currency, instant download.

images.alt: 2027 Budget Planner cover showing the yearly budget dashboard
Monthly budget vs actual view with each category against its plan
Inside the budget planner: setup, transactions and annual view tabs

who_for: You want one place to plan each month and see where the money actually went.
You've tried budgeting apps but don't want to connect your bank account.
You like the 50/30/20 idea and want to see how close your real spending is.

inside.title: Dashboard
inside.text: Income, spending, savings and savings rate for the year, with charts that update as you go.

inside.title: Monthly budget vs actual
inside.text: Pick any month to see every category against its plan. Overspending turns red.

inside.title: 50/30/20 check
inside.text: Your needs / wants / savings split against your own targets.

inside.title: Transactions log
inside.text: Date, category from a dropdown, amount. Type and group fill in automatically.

inside.title: Annual view
inside.text: Every category by month, with the year total against your plan.

inside.title: Setup
inside.text: Up to 8 income sources and 30 expense categories, with your own names and amounts. Change the year in one cell and it works for 2028 and beyond.

products.first_step: On the Setup tab, type your income sources and expense categories with a monthly plan for each.

faq.q: Does it work on a phone?
faq.a: You can log transactions in the Google Sheets or Excel mobile apps. The dashboard is easiest to read on a computer or tablet.

faq.q: Can I add my own categories?
faq.a: Yes. Fill the empty rows on the Setup tab and they appear everywhere automatically.
No. Change the year in one cell on the Setup tab and every date and report follows.

products.name: Debt Payoff Calculator
products.promise: Snowball vs Avalanche side by side: your debt-free date, total interest and a payoff chart.
products.seo_description: Debt payoff calculator spreadsheet for Excel and Google Sheets. Compare debt snowball vs avalanche for up to 8 debts and see your debt-free date. Instant download.

images.alt: Debt Payoff Calculator cover showing the snowball vs avalanche dashboard
Debt payoff dashboard comparing months to debt-free and interest paid for both methods
Inside the debt calculator: debts tab and month-by-month payoff schedule

who_for: You have more than one debt (cards, car loan, personal loan) and want a clear order to pay them off.
You can't decide between the snowball and avalanche methods and want to see both with your own numbers.
You want to know what paying a little extra each month is actually worth.

inside.title: Dashboard
inside.text: Total debt, your debt-free date under each method, interest saved by choosing Avalanche, and a chart of your balance falling over time.

inside.title: Snowball & Avalanche schedules
inside.text: The full month-by-month breakdown for each method: balance, interest, minimum payment, and where every extra payment goes.

inside.title: One extra-payment input
inside.text: Change how much extra you pay each month and every number, date and the chart update instantly.

inside.title: Debts tab
inside.text: Balances, interest rates (APR) and minimum payments for up to 8 debts, over a 15-year horizon.

products.first_step: On the Debts tab, list each debt's balance, APR and minimum payment, plus the extra you can pay each month.

faq.q: Snowball or Avalanche: which should I use?
faq.a: The Dashboard shows both, calculated from your real numbers. Avalanche usually costs less interest overall; Snowball clears small debts fast, which some people find easier to stick with.

faq.q: What if my debt doesn't pay off within 15 years?
faq.a: The Dashboard shows "> 180 months". Add a larger extra payment and the schedule recalculates.

faq.q: Will it tell me to consolidate or refinance?
faq.a: No. It's a planning tool based on the numbers you enter, not a recommendation to refinance, consolidate or take on new debt.

products.name: Savings Goals & Sinking Funds Tracker
products.promise: Track every goal and sinking fund, see which are on track, and when each will be fully funded.
products.seo_description: Savings goals and sinking funds tracker spreadsheet for Excel and Google Sheets. See which goals are on track and when each will be funded. Instant download.

images.alt: Savings Goals Tracker cover showing the savings dashboard
Savings dashboard with progress, on-track flags and projected finish dates for each goal
Inside the savings tracker: goals tab and contributions log

who_for: You're saving for several things at once: an emergency fund, a trip, a laptop.
You use sinking funds for bills you know are coming, like insurance or holidays.
You want an early warning when a goal is falling behind, not just a progress bar.

inside.title: Dashboard
inside.text: Every goal's progress, whether it's on track for its target date, and the month it'll be fully funded at your current pace, plus a progress chart.

inside.title: Goals tab
inside.text: Up to 10 goals or sinking funds: name, target amount, optional target date, starting balance and planned monthly contribution.

inside.title: Contributions log
inside.text: Date, goal from a dropdown, amount. Saved totals update automatically.

inside.title: Works for sinking funds too
inside.text: Car insurance, Christmas, annual subscriptions: anything you set aside for ahead of time.

products.first_step: On the Goals tab, add each goal with its target amount, optional target date and planned monthly amount.

faq.a: Money you set aside gradually for an expense you know is coming, like car insurance or a big annual bill. Add it as a goal with the bill's due date as the target date.

faq.q: What if a goal has no target date?
faq.a: Leave it blank. The Dashboard still tracks progress and shows a projected finish date based on your planned monthly contribution.

products.name: Biweekly Paycheck Budget
products.promise: See which bills come out of which paycheck for the whole year, and spot tight pay periods early.
products.seo_description: Biweekly paycheck budget spreadsheet for Excel and Google Sheets. Maps every bill to the paycheck that pays it, with a running balance for the year. Instant download.

images.alt: Biweekly Paycheck Budget cover showing the paycheck dashboard
Pay period planner listing the bills due in each biweekly pay period
Inside the paycheck budget: setup, planner and paychecks log

who_for: You're paid every two weeks and monthly budgets never quite match your cash flow.
You want to know in advance which paycheck has to cover rent, and which one is tight.
You'd like a running balance for the year without tracking every coffee.

inside.title: Pay Period Planner
inside.text: Every biweekly pay period for the year from one start date: the bills due in each one, what's left after bills, and your running balance.

inside.title: Dashboard
inside.text: Your lowest running balance for the year and exactly which pay period is tightest.

inside.title: Paychecks log (optional)
inside.text: Log actual paychecks as they arrive and the planner uses them instead of your typical amount.

inside.title: Setup
inside.text: Up to 10 monthly bills with name, amount and due day. A bill due on the 31st is handled correctly in shorter months.

products.first_step: On the Setup tab, enter your first payday, your typical paycheck and each monthly bill with its due day.

faq.q: I'm paid weekly, not every two weeks. Does it still work?
faq.a: Reasonably well: treat two weekly paychecks as one pay period and enter their combined amount.
The 27-period planner covers slightly over a year, so any 3-paycheck month on your schedule is included automatically.

products.name: Freelancer Income & Expense Tracker
products.promise: Log client payments and expenses, and see how much to set aside for tax each quarter.
products.seo_description: Freelancer income and expense tracker spreadsheet for Excel and Google Sheets, with a quarterly tax set-aside and deductible expense totals. Instant download.

images.alt: Freelancer Tracker cover showing the freelancer dashboard
Freelancer dashboard with income, expenses, tax set-aside and quarterly breakdown
Inside the freelancer tracker: transactions log and deductible expenses list

who_for: You freelance or run a side business and income arrives unevenly.
You want to know how much of each payment is really yours after expenses and tax.
You'd like deductible expenses already totalled by category at tax time.

inside.title: Dashboard
inside.text: Income, expenses, net income, tax set-aside and real take-home for the year, plus a month-by-month chart.

inside.title: Quarterly breakdown
inside.text: Income, expenses and tax set-aside for each quarter, useful for estimated tax payments.

inside.title: Deductible expense list
inside.text: Every tax-deductible category totalled for the year.

inside.title: Transactions log

inside.title: Setup

products.first_step: On the Setup tab, enter your tax set-aside rate, your clients or income sources, and your expense categories.

faq.q: What tax rate should I use?
faq.a: That's up to you. It should combine your income tax and any self-employment or social-security tax, which vary by country and income. The sheet does the arithmetic; check your rate with a tax professional or your local tax authority.
No. It tracks income and expenses and estimates how much to set aside. It doesn't prepare or file a return.

products.name: Net Worth Tracker
products.promise: Log your accounts once a month and watch your net worth (assets minus debts) trend over time.
products.seo_description: Net worth tracker spreadsheet for Excel and Google Sheets. Log assets and debts monthly and chart your net worth over time. Any currency, instant download.

images.alt: Net Worth Tracker cover showing the net worth dashboard
Net worth dashboard with current net worth, changes and a trend chart
Inside the net worth tracker: accounts tab and monthly snapshots

who_for: You want one number that shows whether you're getting ahead, month to month.
Your money is spread across several accounts, cards and loans.
You want a two-minute monthly habit, not daily tracking.

inside.title: Dashboard
inside.text: Your current net worth, the change since your last and first check-in, and a chart of the trend.

inside.title: Snapshots
inside.text: One row per month, generated from a start date. Fill in each account's balance when you check in.

inside.title: Accounts
inside.text: Up to 15 accounts, each marked as an asset or a liability. Enter debts as what you owe and the tracker subtracts them.

products.first_step: On the Accounts tab, list your accounts and mark each one as an asset or a liability.

faq.q: How often should I update it?
faq.a: Once a month is plenty. Net worth moves slowly, and a monthly check-in shows the real trend without day-to-day noise.

faq.q: What about my house or car?
faq.a: Use a reasonable current value, not what you paid. An online estimate is fine; update it occasionally.

common_faq.a: Yes. Upload the .xlsx file to Google Drive and choose "Open with Google Sheets". Formulas, dropdowns and charts work. You need a free Google account.

common_faq.q: Does it work on a Mac?
common_faq.a: Yes, in Excel for Mac, Excel on the web, or Google Sheets in any browser. No macros or add-ons are used.
